title: Priesthood order rests on councils, keys, and learning one’s duty
setting: In February and March 1835, the church organized the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and the first Seventy. The Twelve were preparing to leave Kirtland on 4 May 1835 for conferences in the eastern states. Joseph Smith gave them this instruction on priesthood sometime between about 1 March and 4 May. Most of verses 60–100 draws on a revelation he dictated in November 1831. It was printed as “On Priesthood” in the 1835 Doctrine and Covenants.
summary: The instruction says the church has two priesthoods, the Melchizedek and the Aaronic. It explains their names and gives each priesthood its keys and duties. It sets out presiding quorums: the Presidency of the Church, the Twelve, and the Seventy. Their decisions must be unanimous and made in righteousness, with appeal possible when a decision is unrighteous. It traces a patriarchal order from Adam through Noah and describes Adam’s last blessing at Adam-ondi-Ahman. Then it details bishops and church councils, including a council that can try the church president. It gives quorum sizes and presidents for deacons, teachers, priests, elders, and the Seventy. It ends: “let every man learn his duty” and act “in all diligence”.

contextNote.title: Order ends in personal duty
contextNote.text: After listing offices, quorums, and councils, the instruction turns to each person. Verse 99 tells “every man” to learn his duty and act in his office. Verse 100 gives the result of neglect: the slothful “shall not be counted worthy to stand”. The long lists before it supply much of what there is to learn. Verses 85–89, for example, describe presidents who teach their quorums their duties. Verse 99 makes that teaching useful only when it is acted on. In this passage, “duty” means the specific work of one’s own office, learned and then done.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 106–108 takes its title, “The Order of the Son of God,” from verse 3. What do verses 85–89 ask quorum presidents to do, and how does that serve the command in verse 99?

jsp.title: Instruction on Priesthood, between circa 1 March and circa 4 May 1835 [D&C 107]

reviewNote: Read all 100 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, circa spring 1835, tied to the organization of the Twelve, with most of vv. 60–100 from a 11 November 1831 revelation. JSP dates it between circa 1 March and circa 4 May 1835; month 1835-04 is a best estimate within that range. JSP notes Oliver Cowdery probably helped prepare it and that the 28 March 1835 date in a later history is likely wrong. Moses is listed because v. 91 compares the church president to him.
